```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      out.width = "100%")
root <- normalizePath(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), mustWork = TRUE)
resolve_output <- function(path) {
  if (!grepl("^(/|[A-Za-z]:)", path)) path <- file.path(root, path)
  normalizePath(path, mustWork = FALSE)
}
sim_out <- resolve_output(params$simulation_output)
real_out <- resolve_output(params$real_paper_output)
require_files <- function(paths, instruction) {
  missing <- paths[!file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(missing)) stop(instruction, "\nMissing: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}
read_table <- function(path) utils::read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE,
                                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
require_files(file.path(sim_out, "completion.csv"),
              "Run figures/run_simulations.R --mode=full before rendering.")
completion <- read_table(file.path(sim_out, "completion.csv"))
parts <- c("sim1", "sim2_linear", "sim2_nonlinear", "sim3")
planned <- c(1600L, 100L, 100L, 1200L)
if (nrow(completion) != length(parts) || anyDuplicated(completion$part) ||
    !setequal(completion$part, parts)) stop("The complete four-part simulation is required.")
completion <- completion[match(parts, completion$part), ]
if (anyNA(completion) || !all(completion$mode == "full") ||
    !all(completion$complete) || !all(completion$planned_jobs == planned) ||
    !all(completion$successful_finite_jobs == planned) ||
    any(completion$failed_jobs != 0 | completion$nonfinite_jobs != 0))
  stop("This report requires completed full simulations; smoke or incomplete results are not accepted.")
require_files(file.path(real_out, "source_manifest.csv"),
              "Run figures/run_real_data.R before rendering.")
manifest <- read_table(file.path(real_out, "source_manifest.csv"))
if (nrow(manifest) != 3L || anyDuplicated(manifest$Dataset) ||
    !setequal(manifest$Dataset, c("pbc", "framingham", "gbsg")))
  stop("The published real-data manifest must contain PBC, Framingham and GBSG2.")
if (!isTRUE(manifest$Horizon_days[manifest$Dataset == "framingham"] == 4380))
  stop("The paper requires the selected 12-year Framingham result.")
if (isTRUE(params$redraw_figures)) {
  run_redraw <- function(section, output_arg) {
    status <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
      c("--vanilla", shQuote(file.path(root, "figures", "redraw_original.R")),
        paste0("--section=", section), shQuote(output_arg)))
    if (status != 0L) stop("Figure redraw failed: ", section)
  }
  run_redraw("simulations", paste0("--sim-output=", sim_out))
  run_redraw("real", paste0("--paper-output=", real_out))
  manifest <- read_table(file.path(real_out, "source_manifest.csv"))
}
sim_figures <- file.path(sim_out, "figures",
  paste0(c("paper.fig4", "paper.fig5", "paper.fig5.2", "paper.fig6"), ".updated.png"))
real_figures <- file.path(real_out, paste0("paper.fig", 1:3, ".png"))
require_files(c(sim_figures, real_figures),
              "Redraw the completed results with figures/redraw_original.R, or render with redraw_figures=TRUE.")
summary_path <- file.path(sim_out, "tables", "metrics_summary.csv")
accuracy_path <- file.path(sim_out, "tables", "sim3_accuracy.csv")
require_files(c(summary_path, accuracy_path), "The simulation summary tables are missing.")
sim_summary <- read_table(summary_path)
accuracy <- read_table(accuracy_path)
if (anyNA(sim_summary[c("completed_jobs", "finite_B", "mean", "empirical_SD", "MCSE")]) ||
    any(sim_summary$completed_jobs != 100 | sim_summary$finite_B != 100))
  stop("Simulation summary cells must contain 100 finite repetitions.")
checks_path <- file.path(real_out, "file_checksums.csv")
require_files(checks_path, "The published real-data integrity record is missing.")
checks <- read_table(checks_path)
checked_paths <- file.path(real_out, checks$File)
require_files(checked_paths, "The published real-data export is incomplete.")
if (!identical(unname(tools::md5sum(checked_paths)), checks$MD5))
  stop("Published real-data files differ from file_checksums.csv; refresh the export.")
real_table_paths <- file.path(real_out,
  c("paper.table2.pbc.csv", "paper.table3.framingham.csv", "paper.table4.gbsg.csv"))
require_files(real_table_paths, "The real-data manuscript tables are missing.")
if (!all(basename(c(real_figures, real_table_paths)) %in% checks$File))
  stop("The integrity record does not cover every displayed real-data figure and table.")
scalar_metrics <- c("pseudo_r2", "brier_score", "harrell_c", "td_auc")
show_simulation <- function(part) {
  x <- sim_summary[sim_summary$part == part &
    sim_summary$Metric %in% c("r_square", "l_square", scalar_metrics),
    c("Model", "Metric", "mean", "empirical_SD", "MCSE", "finite_B")]
  knitr::kable(x, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# Reproduce the paper

This document displays the completed paper results. Rendering reads saved
figures and tables; it does not fit models, run simulations, or append rows to
historical CSV files. The calculation code lives in `analysis/`, and the
manuscript presentation code lives in `figures/`.

From the repository directory, run these commands explicitly when results need
to be recomputed. They load this checkout's package code using `pkgload`.

```{bash reproduce, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Full simulations: substantial computation, with checkpoint resumption.
Rscript --vanilla figures/run_simulations.R --mode=full

# PBC, Framingham and GBSG2, with final figures/tables in one paper folder.
Rscript --vanilla figures/run_real_data.R

# Figures only, using completed results and the selected manuscript style.
Rscript --vanilla figures/redraw_original.R
```

Render this report after the runs finish. `rmarkdown`, `knitr` and Pandoc are
needed in addition to the analysis dependencies listed in the README.

```{r render-instructions, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
rmarkdown::render("paper.code.Rmd", output_dir = "results/report")
# Optional: refresh graphics through the same presentation entry point.
rmarkdown::render("paper.code.Rmd", output_dir = "results/report",
                  params = list(redraw_figures = TRUE))
```

The default inputs are `results/simulations/full/` and
`results/real_data/paper/`; use the document parameters to select other completed
outputs. Results are kept outside Git. A fresh checkout must compute them
before this report can be rendered. Smoke-test results are not accepted here.

# Simulation studies

## Completion and provenance

```{r simulation-completion}
knitr::kable(completion[, c("part", "planned_jobs", "successful_finite_jobs",
                           "failed_jobs", "nonfinite_jobs", "complete")],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

All plotted cells use 100 finite repetitions. Source fingerprints, settings,
R/package versions and RNG configuration are recorded in `configuration.rds`
and `sessionInfo.txt` in the simulation output directory. Models and per-job
checkpoints are retained for resumption. Changing calculation sources or
settings requires a new output directory.

## Simulation 1: effect size and event-time variability

The 16 Weibull scenarios cross four shape settings with four effect sizes.
Each scenario has 10,000 training and 3,000 test subjects. The figure shows the
original effect-size and event-time-variability slices using the selected
`.updated.pdf` layout.

```{r simulation-1, fig.cap="Simulation 1: replication means for the retained scalar metrics."}
knitr::include_graphics(sim_figures[1])
```

The complete replication summaries, empirical SDs and Monte Carlo SEs are in
`tables/metrics_summary.csv` below the simulation output directory.

## Simulation 2: model comparisons

The linear setting compares full and reduced Cox models with lognormal AFT
models at estimated and fixed scale. The nonlinear figure compares RF, Cox and
lognormal AFT. Bars show pseudo R-squared; filled and open dots show the R-squared
and L-squared components, respectively. Other panels show the retained scalar
metrics. The withdrawn metrics are not requested or displayed.

```{r simulation-2-linear, fig.cap="Simulation 2, linear setting."}
knitr::include_graphics(sim_figures[2])
```

```{r simulation-2-linear-table}
show_simulation("sim2_linear")
```

```{r simulation-2-nonlinear, fig.cap="Simulation 2, nonlinear setting."}
knitr::include_graphics(sim_figures[3])
```

```{r simulation-2-nonlinear-table}
# The manuscript figure contains these three models in this order.
x <- sim_summary[sim_summary$part == "sim2_nonlinear" &
  sim_summary$Model %in% c("RF", "Cox", "Ln") &
  sim_summary$Metric %in% c("r_square", "l_square", scalar_metrics),
  c("Model", "Metric", "mean", "empirical_SD", "MCSE", "finite_B")]
x <- x[order(match(x$Model, c("RF", "Cox", "Ln")),
             match(x$Metric, c("r_square", "l_square", scalar_metrics))), ]
knitr::kable(x, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Simulation 3: sample size, censoring and horizon

Sample sizes are 300 and 3,000, censoring settings are 0%, 30% and 70%, and
horizons use the 50th and 90th reference quantiles. Errors use the saved
uncensored, n = 3,000 reference means at each horizon. These are finite-sample
references, not oracle truths. Gray and white boxes retain the selected
manuscript convention for the 90th and 50th quantiles.

```{r simulation-3, fig.cap="Simulation 3: error relative to the saved uncensored reference."}
knitr::include_graphics(sim_figures[4])
```

Bias, RMSE, reference Monte Carlo SEs and repetition counts are available in
`tables/sim3_accuracy.csv`; replication errors and references are retained in
`tables/sim3_errors.csv` and `tables/sim3_references.csv`.

# Real-data illustrations

The source-run manifest selects the current analysis, without a hard-coded run
date or an obsolete result directory. The final table and figure files are
checked against the export's checksum record before display.

## PBC: right-censored survival

The seed-1234567 training/test split compares full Cox, reduced Cox and Weibull
AFT models. Cox predictions use the training fit's baseline hazard and matched
centering. The existing evaluation-grid integration is retained; the repair
does not establish an unrestricted mean beyond observed follow-up.

```{r pbc-table}
knitr::kable(read_table(real_table_paths[1]), digits = 4)
```

```{r pbc-figure, fig.cap="PBC: observed and predicted time summaries."}
knitr::include_graphics(real_figures[1])
```

## Framingham: competing risks, examination 3, 12 years

Time zero is each participant's actual third examination. Models use the same
complete-case cohort and seed-1234567 split. Prediction and evaluation use
`tau = t_star = 4380` days (12 years with 365 days per year). Full follow-up is
used for fitting. The model set contains full and reduced Fine-Gray models and
two cause-specific Weibull AFT specifications.

Competing-risks R-squared uses observed events at their original follow-up
times, a Cox censoring estimate without covariates and a probability floor of
1e-4. Censored rows have zero R-squared weight, including those censored after
the horizon. The lines integrate one minus the hypertension CIF; this is a
restricted no-hypertension summary with competing deaths kept distinct, and a
descriptive illustration rather than a calibration curve.

```{r framingham-table}
knitr::kable(read_table(real_table_paths[2]), digits = 4)
```

```{r framingham-figure, fig.cap="Framingham: third-examination origin and a 12-year horizon, in days."}
knitr::include_graphics(real_figures[2])
```

## GBSG2: case-cohort sampling

The seed-2025 analysis compares Cox models fitted to a case-cohort sample and a
random sample. Sampling weights are calculated on the phase-one cohort before
selecting phase-two subjects. The table uses the current two-phase evaluation.

```{r gbsg-table}
knitr::kable(read_table(real_table_paths[3]), digits = 4)
```

```{r gbsg-figure, fig.cap="GBSG2: case-cohort and random-sample Cox predictions."}
knitr::include_graphics(real_figures[3])
```

# Verification and development record

The package tests include independent moment, probability and prediction
checks for the method changes. Run them independently of paper reproduction:

```{bash package-tests, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
Rscript --vanilla -e 'testthat::test_local(".", reporter="summary")'
```

See `docs/development-2026-10-18.md` for the current development record.
Earlier audits and development plans remain in `docs/superpowers/`; their
status labels refer to the dates recorded there.
